ko.title: 보잉 737 맥스 생산량 월 47대로 정체, 내년 52대 달성 계획에 차질

segments.src: Boeing's long-promised path back to full-speed production of its best-selling jet is proving harder to walk than investors had hoped.
segments.tr: 베스트셀러 제트기의 완전 정상 생산을 향한 보잉의 오랜 약속은 투자자들의 기대보다 더 험난한 길임이 입증되고 있습니다.

segments.src: Chief Executive Kelly Ortberg told analysts that stabilizing 737 Max output at the company's current target rate is taking longer than expected, a disclosure that sent Boeing shares lower and reignited questions about whether the planemaker can hit its next milestone: ramping up to 52 jets a month sometime next year.
segments.tr: 최고경영자(CEO) 켈리 오트버그는 분석가들에게 회사의 현재 목표 생산율로 737 맥스 생산을 안정화하는 데 예상보다 오래 걸리고 있다고 밝혔으며, 이 발표로 보잉 주가가 하락했고 항공기 제작사가 내년 언젠가 월 52대로 증산한다는 다음 이정표를 달성할 수 있을지에 대한 의문이 다시 제기되었습니다.

segments.src: ## Where Production Actually Stands
segments.tr: ## 생산의 실제 현황

segments.src: Boeing has spent much of the past two years trying to climb back to a steady cadence after a mid-air door-plug blowout on an Alaska Airlines Max 9 in January 2024 prompted regulators to cap output while the company overhauled its quality-control processes.
segments.tr: 보잉은 2024년 1월 알래스카 항공 맥스 9의 공중 도어 플러그 이탈 사고 이후 규제 당국이 품질 관리 프로세스를 정비하는 동안 생산량을 제한하도록 조치하면서, 지난 2년 중 대부분의 시간을 안정적인 리듬을 되찾기 위해 노력하는 데 보냈습니다.

segments.src: Since then, the Federal Aviation Administration has allowed Boeing to inch production upward in stages, and the company has said it is currently building around 47 Max jets a month at its Renton, Washington, plant.
segments.tr: 그후 연방항공청(FAA)은 보잉이 단계적으로 생산량을 늘리는 것을 허용했으며, 회사는 현재 워싱턴州 렌턴 공장에서 매월 약 47대의 맥스 제트기를 건조하고 있다고 밝혔습니다.

segments.src: The trouble, according to Ortberg, is not building more airplanes — it is building them at a consistent, repeatable pace without the fits and starts that have plagued the program for years.
segments.tr: 오트버그에 따르면 문제는 더 많은 비행기를 건조하는 것이 아니라, 수년 동안 프로그램을 괴롭혀 온 기복 없이 일관되고 반복 가능한 속도로 건조하는 것입니다.

segments.src: "Stable" has become the operative word inside Boeing's factories: the company wants to prove it can hold a rate for a sustained stretch before asking regulators for permission to go higher, rather than repeating a pattern of surges followed by slowdowns.
segments.tr: "안정적"이라는 단어는 보잉 공장 내부의 핵심 키워드가 되었습니다. 회사는 규제 당국에 더 높은 생산을 허가해 달라고 요청하기 전에, 급증 후 감속이 이어지는 패턴을 반복하는 대신 지속적인 기간 동안 생산율을 유지할 수 있음을 증명하고자 합니다.

segments.src: ## Why the Ramp Keeps Slipping
segments.tr: ## 증산이 계속 지연되는 이유

segments.src: A combination of factors has kept Boeing from locking in that stability.
segments.tr: 여러 요인이 복합적으로 작용하여 보잉은 그 안정을 확보하지 못하고 있습니다.

segments.src: Supply-chain constraints — particularly around fuselage delivery from supplier Spirit AeroSystems, engines, and other structural components — continue to create bottlenecks that ripple through final assembly.
segments.tr: 공급망 제약, 특히 공급업체인 스피릿 에어로시스템즈(Spirit AeroSystems)의 동체 납품, 엔진 및 기타 구조 부품 주변의 제약은 최종 조립 과정 전반에 파급되는 병목 현상을 계속해서 유발하고 있습니다.

segments.src: Boeing has also been deliberately slowing its own internal pace at times to work through traveled work, the industry term for tasks left incomplete as a plane moves down the line, which regulators have flagged as a root cause of past quality lapses.
segments.tr: 또한 보잉은 규제 당국이 과거 품질 부실의 근본 원인으로 지적한, 비행기가 조립 라인을 따라 이동할 때 미완료된 작업인 이동 작업(traveled work)을 해결하기 위해 자체 내부 속도를 고의로 늦추기도 했습니다.

segments.src: Labor availability and training have added further friction.
segments.tr: 노동력 가용성과 교육은 추가적인 마찰을 더했습니다.

segments.src: Boeing brought on thousands of new mechanics and inspectors as part of its quality reset, and integrating that workforce while simultaneously trying to increase output has taken longer than management initially projected.
segments.tr: 보잉은 품질 재설정의 일환으로 수천 명의 새로운 정비사와 검사관을 채용했으며, 생산량을 늘리려는 노력과 동시에 해당 인력을 통합하는 데는 경영진이 처음에 예상했던 것보다 더 오랜 시간이 걸렸습니다.

segments.src: ## What It Means for the 52-a-Month Target
segments.tr: ## 월 52대 목표가 갖는 의미

segments.src: Boeing has repeatedly pointed to 52 Max jets a month as a milestone it hopes to reach next year, a rate the company has not sustained since before the two fatal Max crashes in 2018 and 2019 that led to a 20-month grounding of the fleet.
segments.tr: 보잉은 2018년과 2019년 두 건의 치명적인 맥스 추락 사고로 인해 20개월 동안 항공기 운항이 중단되기 전까지 유지하지 못했던 생산율인 월 52대 맥스를 내년에 달성하고자 하는 이정표로 반복해서 언급해 왔습니다.

segments.src: Ortberg's comments suggest that timeline could be at risk if stabilization at 47 a month takes longer than planned, since the FAA has signaled it will not approve further rate increases until Boeing demonstrates consistent performance at existing levels.
segments.tr: 오트버그의 발언은 FAA가 보잉이 기존 수준에서 일관된 성능을 입증할 때까지 추가적인 생산율 인상을 승인하지 않을 것이라고 신호를 보냈기 때문에, 월 47대에서의 안정화가 계획보다 오래 걸릴 경우 그러한 일정에 차질이 생길 수 있음을 시사합니다.

segments.src: For airline customers waiting on deliveries — including major U.S.
segments.tr: 인도를 기다리는 항공사 고객들(주요 미국 항공사와 맥스 인도에 맞춰 함대 계획을 재구성한 국제 항공사 포함)에게 있어 느린 증산은 밀린 주문이 실제로 언제 도착할지에 대한 지속적인 불확실성을 의미합니다.

segments.src: and international carriers that have restructured fleet plans around Max deliveries — a slower ramp means continued uncertainty about when backlogged orders will actually arrive.
segments.tr: 인도를 기다리는 항공사 고객들(주요 미국 항공사와 맥스 인도에 맞춰 함대 계획을 재구성한 국제 항공사 포함)에게 있어 느린 증산은 밀린 주문이 실제로 언제 도착할지에 대한 지속적인 불확실성을 의미합니다.

segments.src: Boeing's delivery backlog for the Max numbers in the thousands of aircraft, and persistent production delays can affect airline capacity planning, aircraft leasing costs, and route expansion decisions across the industry.
segments.tr: 맥스에 대한 보잉의 인도 적체량은 수천 대에 달하며, 지속적인 생산 지연은 업계 전반의 항공사 용량 계획, 항공기 리스 비용, 노선 확장 결정에 영향을 미칠 수 있습니다.

segments.src: ## Market Reaction
segments.tr: ## 시장 반응

segments.src: Investors responded to Ortberg's remarks by pushing Boeing shares lower, reflecting concern that a slower-than-expected ramp could push out the timeline for the company to generate the free cash flow it has promised.
segments.tr: 투자자들은 오트버그의 발언에 대응하여 보잉 주가를 하락시켰으며, 이는 예상보다 느린 증산으로 인해 회사가 약속한 잉여 현금 흐름 창출 일정이 미뤄질 수 있다는 우려를 반영한 것입니다.

segments.src: Boeing has been working to shore up its balance sheet after years of losses tied to the Max grounding, the COVID-19 downturn in air travel, and production problems on other programs, and steady, growing deliveries of the 737 Max are central to that recovery plan.
segments.tr: 보잉은 맥스 운항 중단, 코로나19로 인한 항공 여행 침체, 기타 프로그램의 생산 문제와 연관된 수년간의 손실 이후 대차대조표를 강화하기 위해 노력해 왔으며, 737 맥스의 꾸준하고 증가하는 인도는 그러한 회복 계획의 핵심입니다.

segments.src: ## The Bigger Picture
segments.tr: ## 더 큰 그림

segments.src: Boeing's leadership has framed the slower ramp as a deliberate trade-off: prioritizing safety and quality discipline over speed, even if that means near-term financial targets slip.
segments.tr: 보잉의 리더십은 단기적인 재무 목표가 미끄러지더라도 속도보다 안전과 품질 규율을 우선시하는 신중한 상충 관계로 느린 증산을 규정했습니다.

segments.src: Whether that approach satisfies investors, airline customers, and regulators alike may depend on how quickly the company can show it has finally broken the boom-and-bust cycle that has defined 737 Max production for much of the past decade.
segments.tr: 이러한 접근 방식이 투자자, 항공사 고객, 규제 당국 모두를 만족시킬 수 있을지는 회사가 지난 10년 동안 737 맥스 생산을 정의해 온 호황과 불황의 주기를 마침내 깨뜨렸다는 것을 얼마나 빨리 보여줄 수 있는지에 달려 있을 수 있습니다.

zh.title: 波音737 Max月产量停滞在47架，为明年达到52架的目标蒙上阴影

segments.src: Boeing's long-promised path back to full-speed production of its best-selling jet is proving harder to walk than investors had hoped.
segments.tr: 波音公司此前承诺的恢复其畅销喷气式飞机全速生产的道路，证明比投资者希望的要艰难得多。

segments.src: Chief Executive Kelly Ortberg told analysts that stabilizing 737 Max output at the company's current target rate is taking longer than expected, a disclosure that sent Boeing shares lower and reignited questions about whether the planemaker can hit its next milestone: ramping up to 52 jets a month sometime next year.
segments.tr: 首席执行官凯利·奥特伯格（Kelly Ortberg）告诉分析师，将737 Max的产量稳定在公司当前的目标水平所需的时间比预期要长，这一披露导致波音股价下跌，并重新引发了人们对这家飞机制造商是否能够实现其下一个里程碑的质疑：即在明年某个时候将产量提升至每月52架。

segments.src: ## Where Production Actually Stands
segments.tr: ## 生产的实际现状

segments.src: Boeing has spent much of the past two years trying to climb back to a steady cadence after a mid-air door-plug blowout on an Alaska Airlines Max 9 in January 2024 prompted regulators to cap output while the company overhauled its quality-control processes.
segments.tr: 在2024年1月阿拉斯加航空一架Max 9发生空中门塞脱落事件导致监管机构限制产量、同时该公司全面整顿其质量控制流程之后，波音公司在过去两年的大部分时间里一直在努力恢复稳定的生产节奏。

segments.src: Since then, the Federal Aviation Administration has allowed Boeing to inch production upward in stages, and the company has said it is currently building around 47 Max jets a month at its Renton, Washington, plant.
segments.tr: 从那以后，美国联邦航空管理局（FAA）允许波音分阶段逐步提高产量，该公司表示目前在其位于华盛顿州伦顿的工厂每月生产约47架Max喷气式飞机。

segments.src: The trouble, according to Ortberg, is not building more airplanes — it is building them at a consistent, repeatable pace without the fits and starts that have plagued the program for years.
segments.tr: 奥特伯格表示，问题不在于制造更多的飞机，而在于以一致、可重复的节奏制造它们，没有多年来一直困扰该项目的起伏不定。

segments.src: "Stable" has become the operative word inside Boeing's factories: the company wants to prove it can hold a rate for a sustained stretch before asking regulators for permission to go higher, rather than repeating a pattern of surges followed by slowdowns.
segments.tr: "稳定"已经成为波音工厂内部的关键词：公司希望证明它能够在持续的一段时间内保持一个速率，然后才向监管机构请求批准提高速率，而不是重复激增随后放缓的模式。

segments.src: ## Why the Ramp Keeps Slipping
segments.tr: ## 为什么产量提升计划不断推迟

segments.src: A combination of factors has kept Boeing from locking in that stability.
segments.tr: 多种因素的组合使得波音无法锁定这种稳定性。

segments.src: Supply-chain constraints — particularly around fuselage delivery from supplier Spirit AeroSystems, engines, and other structural components — continue to create bottlenecks that ripple through final assembly.
segments.tr: 供应链的限制——特别是来自供应商势必锐航空系统公司（Spirit AeroSystems）的机身交付、发动机和其他结构部件——继续产生在最终总装中产生连锁反应的瓶颈。

segments.src: Boeing has also been deliberately slowing its own internal pace at times to work through traveled work, the industry term for tasks left incomplete as a plane moves down the line, which regulators have flagged as a root cause of past quality lapses.
segments.tr: 波音有时还故意放慢自己的内部节奏，以处理遗留工作（即飞机在生产线上移动时未完成的任务的行业术语），监管机构曾指出这是过去质量失误的根本原因。

segments.src: Labor availability and training have added further friction.
segments.tr: 劳动力可用性和培训增加了进一步的摩擦。

segments.src: Boeing brought on thousands of new mechanics and inspectors as part of its quality reset, and integrating that workforce while simultaneously trying to increase output has taken longer than management initially projected.
segments.tr: 作为质量重置的一部分，波音招募了数千名新的机械师和检查员，在试图增加产量的同时整合这支劳动力队伍所花费的时间比管理层最初预计的要长。

segments.src: ## What It Means for the 52-a-Month Target
segments.tr: ## 这对每月52架的目标意味着什么

segments.src: Boeing has repeatedly pointed to 52 Max jets a month as a milestone it hopes to reach next year, a rate the company has not sustained since before the two fatal Max crashes in 2018 and 2019 that led to a 20-month grounding of the fleet.
segments.tr: 波音一再指出每月52架Max是其希望在明年达到的一个里程碑，自2018年和2019年两起致命的Max坠机事故导致该机队停飞20个月之前以来，该公司就再也没有维持过这个速率。

segments.src: Ortberg's comments suggest that timeline could be at risk if stabilization at 47 a month takes longer than planned, since the FAA has signaled it will not approve further rate increases until Boeing demonstrates consistent performance at existing levels.
segments.tr: 奥特伯格的言论表明，如果以每月47架的速度进行稳定需要的时间比计划的长，那么这一时间表可能会面临风险，因为FAA已经表示，在波音证明现有水平表现一致之前，它不会批准进一步的速率提高。

segments.src: For airline customers waiting on deliveries — including major U.S.
segments.tr: 对于等待交货的航空公司客户——包括围绕Max交付重组机队计划的主要美国和国际航空公司——

segments.src: and international carriers that have restructured fleet plans around Max deliveries — a slower ramp means continued uncertainty about when backlogged orders will actually arrive.
segments.tr: 生产提速放缓意味着积压订单究竟何时到达仍存在持续的不确定性。

segments.tr: 波音的Max交付积压订单达数千架，持续的生产延误会影响整个行业的航空公司产能规划、飞机租赁成本和航线扩张决策。

segments.src: ## Market Reaction
segments.tr: ## 市场反应

segments.src: Investors responded to Ortberg's remarks by pushing Boeing shares lower, reflecting concern that a slower-than-expected ramp could push out the timeline for the company to generate the free cash flow it has promised.
segments.tr: 投资者对奥特伯格的言论作出反应，推动波音股价下跌，这反映出人们担心比预期慢的提速可能会推迟该公司产生其承诺的自由现金流的时间表。

segments.src: Boeing has been working to shore up its balance sheet after years of losses tied to the Max grounding, the COVID-19 downturn in air travel, and production problems on other programs, and steady, growing deliveries of the 737 Max are central to that recovery plan.
segments.tr: 在经历与Max停飞、新冠疫情航空旅行低迷以及其他项目生产问题相关的多年亏损后，波音一直在努力巩固其资产负债表，而737 Max稳定、不断增长的交付量是该复苏计划的核心。

segments.src: ## The Bigger Picture
segments.tr: ## 更宏观的视角

segments.src: Boeing's leadership has framed the slower ramp as a deliberate trade-off: prioritizing safety and quality discipline over speed, even if that means near-term financial targets slip.
segments.tr: 波音领导层将提速放缓描述为一种刻意的权衡：将安全和质量纪律置于速度之上，即使这意味着近期财务目标的滑落。

segments.src: Whether that approach satisfies investors, airline customers, and regulators alike may depend on how quickly the company can show it has finally broken the boom-and-bust cycle that has defined 737 Max production for much of the past decade.
segments.tr: 这种方法是否能让投资者、航空公司客户和监管机构同样满意，可能取决于该公司能以多快速度证明它终于打破了在过去十年大部分时间里定义了737 Max生产的繁荣与萧条的周期。

es.title: La producción del 737 Max de Boeing se estanca en 47 al mes, lo que nubla los planes de alcanzar las 52 unidades el próximo año

segments.src: Boeing's long-promised path back to full-speed production of its best-selling jet is proving harder to walk than investors had hoped.
segments.tr: El camino prometido desde hace tiempo por Boeing para regresar a la producción a toda velocidad de su avión más vendido está resultando más difícil de recorrer de lo que esperaban los inversores.

segments.src: Chief Executive Kelly Ortberg told analysts that stabilizing 737 Max output at the company's current target rate is taking longer than expected, a disclosure that sent Boeing shares lower and reignited questions about whether the planemaker can hit its next milestone: ramping up to 52 jets a month sometime next year.
segments.tr: El director ejecutivo Kelly Ortberg dijo a los analistas que estabilizar la producción del 737 Max en la tasa objetivo actual de la empresa está tomando más tiempo de lo esperado, una revelación que hizo caer las acciones de Boeing y reavivó las dudas sobre si el fabricante de aviones podrá alcanzar su próximo hito: aumentar a 52 aviones al mes en algún momento del próximo año.

segments.src: ## Where Production Actually Stands
segments.tr: ## Dónde se encuentra realmente la producción

segments.src: Boeing has spent much of the past two years trying to climb back to a steady cadence after a mid-air door-plug blowout on an Alaska Airlines Max 9 in January 2024 prompted regulators to cap output while the company overhauled its quality-control processes.
segments.tr: Boeing ha pasado gran parte de los últimos dos años intentando recuperar un ritmo constante después de que el desprendimiento del tapón de la puerta en pleno vuelo en un Max 9 de Alaska Airlines en enero de 2024 llevara a los reguladores a limitar la producción mientras la empresa revisaba sus procesos de control de calidad.

segments.src: Since then, the Federal Aviation Administration has allowed Boeing to inch production upward in stages, and the company has said it is currently building around 47 Max jets a month at its Renton, Washington, plant.
segments.tr: Desde entonces, la Administración Federal de Aviación ha permitido a Boeing aumentar la producción gradualmente por etapas, y la empresa ha dicho que actualmente está construyendo alrededor de 47 aviones Max al mes en su planta de Renton, Washington.

segments.src: The trouble, according to Ortberg, is not building more airplanes — it is building them at a consistent, repeatable pace without the fits and starts that have plagued the program for years.
segments.tr: El problema, según Ortberg, no es construir más aviones; es construirlos a un ritmo constante y repetible sin los altibajos que han plagado el programa durante años.

segments.src: "Stable" has become the operative word inside Boeing's factories: the company wants to prove it can hold a rate for a sustained stretch before asking regulators for permission to go higher, rather than repeating a pattern of surges followed by slowdowns.
segments.tr: "Estable" se ha convertido en la palabra clave dentro de las fábricas de Boeing: la empresa quiere demostrar que puede mantener una tasa durante un periodo prolongado antes de pedir permiso a los reguladores para subir más, en lugar de repetir un patrón de aumentos repentinos seguidos de desaceleraciones.

segments.src: ## Why the Ramp Keeps Slipping
segments.tr: ## Por qué el aumento sigue retrasándose

segments.src: A combination of factors has kept Boeing from locking in that stability.
segments.tr: Una combinación de factores ha impedido que Boeing se consolide en esa estabilidad.

segments.src: Supply-chain constraints — particularly around fuselage delivery from supplier Spirit AeroSystems, engines, and other structural components — continue to create bottlenecks that ripple through final assembly.
segments.tr: Las restricciones en la cadena de suministro —particularmente en torno a la entrega de fuselajes por parte del proveedor Spirit AeroSystems, motores y otros componentes estructurales— continúan creando cuellos de botella que repercuten en el ensamblaje final.

segments.src: Boeing has also been deliberately slowing its own internal pace at times to work through traveled work, the industry term for tasks left incomplete as a plane moves down the line, which regulators have flagged as a root cause of past quality lapses.
segments.tr: Boeing también ha estado frenando deliberadamente su propio ritmo interno a veces para resolver el trabajo diferido (traveled work), el término de la industria para las tareas que quedan incompletas a medida que el avión avanza en la línea de montaje, lo que los reguladores han señalado como la causa principal de las fallas de calidad pasadas.

segments.src: Labor availability and training have added further friction.
segments.tr: La disponibilidad de mano de obra y la capacitación han añadido más fricción.

segments.src: Boeing brought on thousands of new mechanics and inspectors as part of its quality reset, and integrating that workforce while simultaneously trying to increase output has taken longer than management initially projected.
segments.tr: Boeing incorporó a miles de nuevos mecánicos e inspectores como parte de su reinicio de calidad, e integrar a esa fuerza laboral mientras intenta simultáneamente aumentar la producción ha llevado más tiempo del que la dirección proyectó inicialmente.

segments.src: Chief Executive Kelly Ortberg told analysts that stabilizing 737 Max output at the company's current target rate is taking longer than expected, a disclosure that sent Boeing shares lower and reignited questions about whether the planemaker can hit its next milestone: ramping up to 52 jets a month sometime next year.
segments.tr: Le directeur général Kelly Ortberg a déclaré aux analystes que la stabilisation de la production du 737 Max au rythme cible actuel de l'entreprise prend plus de temps que prévu, une révélation qui a fait chuter les actions de Boeing et a relancé les questions sur la capacité du constructeur aéronautique à atteindre sa prochaine étape : passer à 52 jets par mois dans le courant de l'année prochaine.

segments.src: ## Where Production Actually Stands
segments.tr: ## Où en est réellement la production

segments.src: Boeing has spent much of the past two years trying to climb back to a steady cadence after a mid-air door-plug blowout on an Alaska Airlines Max 9 in January 2024 prompted regulators to cap output while the company overhauled its quality-control processes.
segments.tr: Boeing a passé une grande partie des deux dernières années à essayer de retrouver un rythme régulier après qu'une explosion de porte-bouchon en plein vol sur un Max 9 d'Alaska Airlines en janvier 2024 a incité les régulateurs à plafonner la production pendant que l'entreprise remaniait ses processus de contrôle de la qualité.

segments.src: Since then, the Federal Aviation Administration has allowed Boeing to inch production upward in stages, and the company has said it is currently building around 47 Max jets a month at its Renton, Washington, plant.
segments.tr: Depuis lors, la Federal Aviation Administration a autorisé Boeing à augmenter progressivement sa production, et l'entreprise a déclaré qu'elle construisait actuellement environ 47 jets Max par mois dans son usine de Renton, dans l'État de Washington.

segments.src: The trouble, according to Ortberg, is not building more airplanes — it is building them at a consistent, repeatable pace without the fits and starts that have plagued the program for years.
segments.tr: Le problème, selon M. Ortberg, n'est pas de construire plus d'avions, mais de les construire à un rythme cohérent et reproductible, sans les à-coups qui ont plombé le programme pendant des années.

segments.src: "Stable" has become the operative word inside Boeing's factories: the company wants to prove it can hold a rate for a sustained stretch before asking regulators for permission to go higher, rather than repeating a pattern of surges followed by slowdowns.
segments.tr: "Stable" est devenu le mot d'ordre dans les usines de Boeing : l'entreprise veut prouver qu'elle peut maintenir un rythme pendant une période prolongée avant de demander aux régulateurs l'autorisation d'aller plus haut, plutôt que de répéter un schéma de hausses suivies de ralentissements.

segments.src: ## Why the Ramp Keeps Slipping
segments.tr: ## Pourquoi la montée en cadence ne cesse de glisser

segments.src: A combination of factors has kept Boeing from locking in that stability.
segments.tr: Une combinaison de facteurs a empêché Boeing de verrouiller cette stabilité.

segments.src: Supply-chain constraints — particularly around fuselage delivery from supplier Spirit AeroSystems, engines, and other structural components — continue to create bottlenecks that ripple through final assembly.
segments.tr: Les contraintes de la chaîne d'approvisionnement, en particulier concernant la livraison des fuselages par le fournisseur Spirit AeroSystems, les moteurs et d'autres composants structurels, continuent de créer des goulots d'étranglement qui se répercutent sur l'assemblage final.

segments.src: Boeing has also been deliberately slowing its own internal pace at times to work through traveled work, the industry term for tasks left incomplete as a plane moves down the line, which regulators have flagged as a root cause of past quality lapses.
segments.tr: Boeing a également ralenti délibérément son propre rythme interne à certains moments pour traiter le travail accumulé en cours de route (traveled work), le terme de l'industrie pour les tâches laissées inachevées lorsqu'un avion avance sur la chaîne, que les régulateurs ont signalé comme une cause profonde des défaillances de qualité passées.

segments.src: Labor availability and training have added further friction.
segments.tr: La disponibilité de la main-d'œuvre et la formation ont ajouté des frictions supplémentaires.

segments.src: Boeing brought on thousands of new mechanics and inspectors as part of its quality reset, and integrating that workforce while simultaneously trying to increase output has taken longer than management initially projected.
segments.tr: Boeing a embauché des milliers de nouveaux mécaniciens et inspecteurs dans le cadre de sa remise à niveau de la qualité, et l'intégration de cette main-d'œuvre tout en essayant simultanément d'augmenter la production a pris plus de temps que la direction ne l'avait initialement prévu.

segments.src: ## What It Means for the 52-a-Month Target
segments.tr: ## Ce que cela signifie pour l'objectif de 52 par mois

segments.src: Boeing has repeatedly pointed to 52 Max jets a month as a milestone it hopes to reach next year, a rate the company has not sustained since before the two fatal Max crashes in 2018 and 2019 that led to a 20-month grounding of the fleet.
segments.tr: Boeing a répété à plusieurs reprises que l'objectif de 52 jets Max par mois était une étape qu'il espérait atteindre l'année prochaine, un rythme que l'entreprise n'a pas soutenu depuis avant les deux accidents mortels du Max en 2018 et 2019 qui ont conduit à une immobilisation au sol de la flotte pendant 20 mois.

segments.src: Ortberg's comments suggest that timeline could be at risk if stabilization at 47 a month takes longer than planned, since the FAA has signaled it will not approve further rate increases until Boeing demonstrates consistent performance at existing levels.
segments.tr: Les commentaires de M. Ortberg suggèrent que ce calendrier pourrait être menacé si la stabilisation à 47 par mois prend plus de temps que prévu, la FAA ayant indiqué qu'elle n'approuverait pas de nouvelles augmentations de cadence tant que Boeing n'aura pas démontré des performances constantes aux niveaux existants.

segments.src: For airline customers waiting on deliveries — including major U.S.
segments.tr: Pour les compagnies aériennes clientes qui attendent des livraisons, y compris les principaux transporteurs américains

segments.src: and international carriers that have restructured fleet plans around Max deliveries — a slower ramp means continued uncertainty about when backlogged orders will actually arrive.
segments.tr: et internationaux qui ont restructuré leurs plans de flotte autour des livraisons de Max, une montée en cadence plus lente signifie une incertitude continue quant au moment où les commandes en retard arriveront réellement.

segments.src: Boeing's delivery backlog for the Max numbers in the thousands of aircraft, and persistent production delays can affect airline capacity planning, aircraft leasing costs, and route expansion decisions across the industry.
segments.tr: Le carnet de commandes de livraison de Boeing pour le Max se chiffre par milliers d'appareils, et les retards de production persistants peuvent affecter la planification de la capacité des compagnies aériennes, les coûts de location d'avions et les décisions d'expansion des routes dans toute l'industrie.

segments.src: ## Market Reaction
segments.tr: ## Réaction du marché

segments.src: Investors responded to Ortberg's remarks by pushing Boeing shares lower, reflecting concern that a slower-than-expected ramp could push out the timeline for the company to generate the free cash flow it has promised.
segments.tr: Les investisseurs ont réagi aux remarques de M. Ortberg en faisant baisser les actions de Boeing, reflétant la crainte qu'une montée en cadence plus lente que prévu ne repousse le calendrier pour l'entreprise afin de générer le flux de trésorerie disponible qu'elle a promis.

segments.src: Boeing has been working to shore up its balance sheet after years of losses tied to the Max grounding, the COVID-19 downturn in air travel, and production problems on other programs, and steady, growing deliveries of the 737 Max are central to that recovery plan.
segments.tr: Boeing s'efforce de consolider son bilan après des années de pertes liées à l'immobilisation au sol du Max, au ralentissement du transport aérien dû au COVID-19 et à des problèmes de production sur d'autres programmes, et des livraisons régulières et croissantes du 737 Max sont au cœur de ce plan de reprise.

segments.src: ## The Bigger Picture
segments.tr: ## La vue d'ensemble

segments.src: Boeing's leadership has framed the slower ramp as a deliberate trade-off: prioritizing safety and quality discipline over speed, even if that means near-term financial targets slip.
segments.tr: La direction de Boeing a présenté le ralentissement de la montée en cadence comme un compromis délibéré : donner la priorité à la sécurité et à la discipline de qualité plutôt qu'à la vitesse, même si cela signifie que les objectifs financiers à court terme glissent.

segments.src: Whether that approach satisfies investors, airline customers, and regulators alike may depend on how quickly the company can show it has finally broken the boom-and-bust cycle that has defined 737 Max production for much of the past decade.
segments.tr: La question de savoir si cette approche satisfait les investisseurs, les clients des compagnies aériennes et les régulateurs dépendra de la rapidité avec laquelle l'entreprise pourra montrer qu'elle a enfin brisé le cycle de boom et de récession qui a caractérisé la production du 737 Max pendant une grande partie de la dernière décennie.

ja.title: ボーイングの737 Max生産、月47機で頭打ちに――来年の52機達成計画に暗雲

segments.src: Boeing's long-promised path back to full-speed production of its best-selling jet is proving harder to walk than investors had hoped.
segments.tr: ボーイングが長年約束してきた、ベストセラー機のフルスピード生産への復帰への道のりは、投資家が期待していたよりも歩みのが難しいことが証明されている。

segments.src: Chief Executive Kelly Ortberg told analysts that stabilizing 737 Max output at the company's current target rate is taking longer than expected, a disclosure that sent Boeing shares lower and reignited questions about whether the planemaker can hit its next milestone: ramping up to 52 jets a month sometime next year.
segments.tr: 最高経営責任者（CEO）のケリー・オートバーグ氏はアナリストに対し、同社の現在の目標ペースでの737 Maxの生産安定化には予想以上に時間がかかっていると語った。この発表によりボーイング株は下落し、同社が次のマイルストーンである「来年中の月産52機への引き上げ」を達成できるかどうかについて、再び疑問の声が上がっている。

segments.src: ## Where Production Actually Stands
segments.tr: ## 現在の実際の生産状況

segments.src: Boeing has spent much of the past two years trying to climb back to a steady cadence after a mid-air door-plug blowout on an Alaska Airlines Max 9 in January 2024 prompted regulators to cap output while the company overhauled its quality-control processes.
segments.tr: ボーイングは、2024年1月にアラスカ航空のMax 9で発生した飛行中のドアプラグ吹き飛び事故を受け、規制当局が品質管理プロセスの見直し期間中の生産上限設定を義務付けて以来、過去2年間の大部分を安定したペースへの復帰に向けた努力に費やしてきた。

segments.src: Since then, the Federal Aviation Administration has allowed Boeing to inch production upward in stages, and the company has said it is currently building around 47 Max jets a month at its Renton, Washington, plant.
segments.tr: それ以来、連邦航空局（FAA）はボーイングが段階的に生産をわずかに引き上げることを許可しており、同社は現在、ワシントン州レントンの工場で737 Maxを月産約47機ペースで製造していると述べている。

segments.src: The trouble, according to Ortberg, is not building more airplanes — it is building them at a consistent, repeatable pace without the fits and starts that have plagued the program for years.
segments.tr: オートバーグ氏によれば、問題はより多くの飛行機を建造することではなく、長年このプログラムを悩ませてきた中断や停滞なしに、一貫した再現性のあるペースで建造することにある。

segments.src: "Stable" has become the operative word inside Boeing's factories: the company wants to prove it can hold a rate for a sustained stretch before asking regulators for permission to go higher, rather than repeating a pattern of surges followed by slowdowns.
segments.tr: 「安定」はボーイングの工場内におけるキーワードとなっている。同社は、急増とその後の減速というパターンの繰り返しではなく、規制当局に追加引き上げの許可を求める前に、持続的な期間にわたって生産ペースを維持できることを証明したいと考えている。

segments.src: ## Why the Ramp Keeps Slipping
segments.tr: ## なぜ増産ペースが落ち続けるのか

segments.src: A combination of factors has kept Boeing from locking in that stability.
segments.tr: いくつかの要因が重なり、ボーイングはその安定性を確保できずにいる。

segments.src: Supply-chain constraints — particularly around fuselage delivery from supplier Spirit AeroSystems, engines, and other structural components — continue to create bottlenecks that ripple through final assembly.
segments.tr: サプライチェーンの制約――特にサプライヤーであるスピリット・エアロシステムズからの胴体納入、エンジン、その他の構造部品に関するものが――最終組み立てに波及するボトルネックを生み出し続けている。

segments.src: Boeing has also been deliberately slowing its own internal pace at times to work through traveled work, the industry term for tasks left incomplete as a plane moves down the line, which regulators have flagged as a root cause of past quality lapses.
segments.tr: またボーイングは、トラベルドワーク（飛行機がラインを進むにつれて未完成のまま残された作業を指す業界用語で、規制当局が過去の品質ミスの根本原因として指摘しているもの）を解消するため、自社の内部ペースを意図的に落とすことさえあった。

segments.src: Labor availability and training have added further friction.
segments.tr: 労働力の確保とトレーニングがさらなる摩擦を生んでいる。

segments.src: Boeing brought on thousands of new mechanics and inspectors as part of its quality reset, and integrating that workforce while simultaneously trying to increase output has taken longer than management initially projected.
segments.tr: ボーイングは品質リセットの一環として何千人もの新しい整備士や検査員を採用したが、生産台数を増やそうと同時に試みる中でその労働力を統合するには、経営陣が最初に予測したよりも長い時間がかかっている。

segments.src: ## What It Means for the 52-a-Month Target
segments.tr: ## 月産52機目標への意味

segments.src: Boeing has repeatedly pointed to 52 Max jets a month as a milestone it hopes to reach next year, a rate the company has not sustained since before the two fatal Max crashes in 2018 and 2019 that led to a 20-month grounding of the fleet.
segments.tr: ボーイングは、来年達成したいマイルストーンとして月産52機のMaxを繰り返し挙げてきた。これは、機体の20か月にわたる運航停止につながった2018年と2019年の2度の致命的なMax墜落事故以来、同社が維持したことのないペースである。

segments.src: Ortberg's comments suggest that timeline could be at risk if stabilization at 47 a month takes longer than planned, since the FAA has signaled it will not approve further rate increases until Boeing demonstrates consistent performance at existing levels.
segments.tr: オートバーグ氏の発言は、月産47機での安定化が計画より長引いた場合、そのタイムラインが危険にさらされる可能性を示唆している。FAAは、ボーイングが現行のレベルで一貫したパフォーマンスを発揮するのを実証するまで、さらなる増産を承認しないと示しているからだ。

segments.src: For airline customers waiting on deliveries — including major U.S.
segments.tr: 納入を待ち望んでいる航空会社顧客にとって――Maxの納入を中心にフリート計画を再構築した米国の主要航空会社や国際的な航空会社を含め――

segments.src: and international carriers that have restructured fleet plans around Max deliveries — a slower ramp means continued uncertainty about when backlogged orders will actually arrive.
segments.tr: 増産の遅れは、受注残が実際にいつ到着するのかについての不確実性が続くことを意味する。

segments.src: Boeing's delivery backlog for the Max numbers in the thousands of aircraft, and persistent production delays can affect airline capacity planning, aircraft leasing costs, and route expansion decisions across the industry.
segments.tr: Maxに対するボーイングの納入バックログは数千機に上り、持続的な生産の遅れは、業界全体の航空会社のキャパシティ計画、航空機のリース費用、および路線拡大の決定に影響を与える可能性がある。

segments.src: ## Market Reaction
segments.tr: ## 市場の反応

segments.src: Investors responded to Ortberg's remarks by pushing Boeing shares lower, reflecting concern that a slower-than-expected ramp could push out the timeline for the company to generate the free cash flow it has promised.
segments.tr: 投資家はオートバーグ氏の発言に対しボーイング株を売ることで反応し、予想よりも遅い増産ペースが、同社が約束したフリーキャッシュフローを創出するタイムラインを先送りさせるのではないかという懸念を反映した。

segments.src: Boeing has been working to shore up its balance sheet after years of losses tied to the Max grounding, the COVID-19 downturn in air travel, and production problems on other programs, and steady, growing deliveries of the 737 Max are central to that recovery plan.
segments.tr: ボーイングは、Maxの運航停止、COVID-19による空の旅の落ち込み、およびその他のプログラムでの生産問題に起因する長年の損失の後、バランスシートの立て直しに取り組んできただが、737 Maxの着実で増加する納入はその回復計画の中心となっている。

segments.src: ## The Bigger Picture
segments.tr: ## より大きな文脈

segments.src: Boeing's leadership has framed the slower ramp as a deliberate trade-off: prioritizing safety and quality discipline over speed, even if that means near-term financial targets slip.
segments.tr: ボーイングの経営陣は、増産の遅れを意図的なトレードオフとして位置づけている。すなわち、たとえ短期的な財務目標が狂うことになっても、スピードよりも安全性と品質規律を優先させるというものだ。

segments.src: Whether that approach satisfies investors, airline customers, and regulators alike may depend on how quickly the company can show it has finally broken the boom-and-bust cycle that has defined 737 Max production for much of the past decade.
segments.tr: このアプローチが投資家、航空会社顧客、そして規制当局を同様に満足させるかどうかは、過去10年の大部分において737 Maxの生産を規定してきた好不況のサイクルを同社がついに断ち切ったことをどれほど迅速に示せるかにかかっているかもしれない。

segments.tr: Các hạn chế về chuỗi cung ứng — đặc biệt là việc giao thân máy bay từ nhà cung cấp Spirit AeroSystems, động cơ và các thành phần cấu trúc khác — tiếp tục tạo ra các điểm nghẽn lan truyền đến quá trình lắp ráp cuối cùng.

segments.src: Boeing has also been deliberately slowing its own internal pace at times to work through traveled work, the industry term for tasks left incomplete as a plane moves down the line, which regulators have flagged as a root cause of past quality lapses.
segments.tr: Boeing cũng đã chủ động làm chậm nhịp độ nội bộ của mình ở một số thời điểm để xử lý công việc dồn lại (traveled work), thuật ngữ ngành chỉ các nhiệm vụ chưa hoàn thành khi máy bay di chuyển tiếp trên dây chuyền, điều mà các cơ quan quản lý đã chỉ ra là nguyên nhân gốc rễ của những thiếu sót về chất lượng trong quá khứ.

segments.src: Labor availability and training have added further friction.
segments.tr: Nguồn lực lao động và công tác đào tạo cũng gây thêm lực cản.

segments.src: Boeing brought on thousands of new mechanics and inspectors as part of its quality reset, and integrating that workforce while simultaneously trying to increase output has taken longer than management initially projected.
segments.tr: Boeing đã tuyển dụng hàng nghìn thợ máy và kiểm định viên mới như một phần của việc tái thiết lập chất lượng, và việc tích hợp lực lượng lao động đó đồng thời với nỗ lực tăng sản lượng đã mất nhiều thời gian hơn so với dự kiến ban đầu của ban quản lý.

segments.src: ## What It Means for the 52-a-Month Target
segments.tr: ## Ý nghĩa đối với mục tiêu 52 chiếc một tháng

segments.src: Boeing has repeatedly pointed to 52 Max jets a month as a milestone it hopes to reach next year, a rate the company has not sustained since before the two fatal Max crashes in 2018 and 2019 that led to a 20-month grounding of the fleet.
segments.tr: Boeing đã liên tục chỉ ra mức 52 máy bay Max một tháng là cột mốc mà họ hy vọng sẽ đạt được vào năm tới, một mức sản lượng mà công ty chưa từng duy trì kể từ trước hai tai nạn thảm khốc của Max vào năm 2018 và 2019 khiến toàn bộ dòng máy bay này bị cấm bay trong 20 tháng.

segments.src: Ortberg's comments suggest that timeline could be at risk if stabilization at 47 a month takes longer than planned, since the FAA has signaled it will not approve further rate increases until Boeing demonstrates consistent performance at existing levels.
segments.tr: Các bình luận của Ortberg cho thấy mốc thời gian đó có thể gặp rủi ro nếu việc ổn định ở mức 47 chiếc một tháng mất nhiều thời gian hơn kế hoạch, vì FAA đã phát tín hiệu rằng họ sẽ không phê duyệt các đợt tăng sản lượng tiếp theo cho đến khi Boeing chứng minh được hiệu suất ổn định ở các mức hiện tại.

segments.src: For airline customers waiting on deliveries — including major U.S.
segments.tr: Đối với các khách hàng hãng hàng không đang chờ nhận hàng — bao gồm các hãng hàng không lớn của Mỹ

segments.src: and international carriers that have restructured fleet plans around Max deliveries — a slower ramp means continued uncertainty about when backlogged orders will actually arrive.
segments.tr: và quốc tế vốn đã tái cấu trúc kế hoạch đội bay xung quanh các đợt giao hàng Max — đợt tăng sản lượng chậm hơn đồng nghĩa với việc tiếp tục bất ổn về thời điểm các đơn đặt hàng tồn đọng thực sự được giao.

segments.src: Boeing's delivery backlog for the Max numbers in the thousands of aircraft, and persistent production delays can affect airline capacity planning, aircraft leasing costs, and route expansion decisions across the industry.
segments.tr: Số lượng đơn hàng tồn đọng giao Max của Boeing lên tới hàng nghìn máy bay, và sự chậm trễ sản xuất kéo dài có thể ảnh hưởng đến kế hoạch năng lực của hãng hàng không, chi phí thuê máy bay và các quyết định mở rộng đường bay trong toàn ngành.

segments.src: ## Market Reaction
segments.tr: ## Phản ứng của thị trường

segments.src: Investors responded to Ortberg's remarks by pushing Boeing shares lower, reflecting concern that a slower-than-expected ramp could push out the timeline for the company to generate the free cash flow it has promised.
segments.tr: Các nhà đầu tư đã phản ứng với nhận định của Ortberg bằng cách đẩy cổ phiếu Boeing xuống thấp hơn, phản ánh sự lo ngại rằng tiến độ tăng sản lượng chậm hơn dự kiến có thể kéo dài thời gian để công ty tạo ra dòng tiền tự do như đã hứa.

segments.src: Boeing has been working to shore up its balance sheet after years of losses tied to the Max grounding, the COVID-19 downturn in air travel, and production problems on other programs, and steady, growing deliveries of the 737 Max are central to that recovery plan.
segments.tr: Boeing đã và đang nỗ lực củng cố bảng cân đối kế toán sau nhiều năm thua lỗ gắn liền với việc dòng Max bị cấm bay, sự suy giảm của ngành du lịch hàng không do COVID-19 và các vấn đề sản xuất trên các chương trình khác; việc giao hàng 737 Max ổn định và tăng trưởng là trung tâm của kế hoạch phục hồi đó.

segments.src: ## The Bigger Picture
segments.tr: ## Bức tranh toàn cảnh hơn

segments.src: Boeing's leadership has framed the slower ramp as a deliberate trade-off: prioritizing safety and quality discipline over speed, even if that means near-term financial targets slip.
segments.tr: Lãnh đạo của Boeing đã coi việc tăng sản lượng chậm hơn là một sự đánh đổi có tính toán: ưu tiên nguyên tắc an toàn và chất lượng hơn tốc độ, ngay cả khi điều đó có nghĩa là các mục tiêu tài chính trong ngắn hạn bị trượt.

segments.src: Whether that approach satisfies investors, airline customers, and regulators alike may depend on how quickly the company can show it has finally broken the boom-and-bust cycle that has defined 737 Max production for much of the past decade.
segments.tr: Liệu phương pháp đó có làm hài lòng các nhà đầu tư, khách hàng hãng hàng không và các cơ quan quản lý hay không có thể phụ thuộc vào việc công ty có thể nhanh chóng chứng minh rằng họ đã thoát khỏi chu kỳ bùng nổ rồi suy ngoái vốn đã định hình quá trình sản xuất 737 Max trong phần lớn thập kỷ qua hay không.
